# Duplicate & Merge

`customer_support.intake_and_triage.duplicate_and_merge` · v0.1.0 · **draft** · **STUB**

**Is this the same problem we already have, and what is lost if I merge them?**


> Recognising when several tickets are one problem, and deciding which of them is allowed to survive. Merging is destructive in a way that is easy to underestimate: it collapses separate requesters, clocks, entitlements and notification threads into one, so a merge performed for tidiness can quietly break a promise made to whoever was not the survivor. The counter-risk is worse, though — unmerged duplicates hide the fact that a fault is spreading, and contact volume against a single issue is usually the only blast-radius evidence anyone has before engineering reproduces anything. The right instinct is to relate aggressively and merge conservatively: linking is reversible and preserves every clock, merging is neither.

Promote by writing the link-versus-merge distinction as a decision_framework first, since everything else depends on it: same requester and same symptom is a merge candidate, different requesters and the same symptom is almost always a link to a shared Issue instead. failure_modes should include merging across accounts (which discloses one customer to another in the wrong tooling), merging away the reopened ticket rather than the newer one, and the opposite failure of leaving duplicates apart so long that severity is discovered by engineering rather than by the queue.
